paths.audience: Sponsors, governance leads and risk owners
paths.goal: Decide whether and how to adopt the guide

steps.outcome: Establish scope, non-claims and authority model
Choose an adoption stage and entry gate
Fix assurance and disclosure boundaries
Assign controls and residual-risk ownership
Apply an evidence-backed stop/go gate

paths.audience: Architects and issuer, wallet, verifier, registry or agent engineers

steps.outcome: Establish system boundaries and component relationships
Fix predicate assurance and disclosure constraints
Apply role-specific requirements and interface contracts
Resolve cross-specification authority and evidence dependencies
Produce repeatable conformance evidence

paths.goal: Deploy and sustain a controlled production system

steps.outcome: Confirm topology and security baseline
Establish monitoring, incident and recovery playbooks
Define cryptoperiod and migration triggers
Trace threats, controls, metrics and residual risk
Produce production-readiness evidence

paths.goal: Independently reconstruct and test assurance claims

steps.outcome: Define assessment scope and evidence classes
Trace claims to guidance and evidence
Select adverse and lifecycle samples
Verify repeatable test evidence and dispositions
Distinguish ratified, local and unresolved decisions

paths.goal: Resolve cross-specification assumptions in the correct governance plane

steps.outcome: Identify dependency direction and owning authority
Review findings assigned to the narrowest legitimate control plane
Determine local versus upstream decision status
Identify the appropriate upstream resolution target
